example.title: McFarland Gap Road Culvert
example.place: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Fort Oglethorpe, Catoosa County, GA

brief: Low twin-barrel masonry culvert under a two-lane paved road: two small segmental arches of about 5 ft span side by side in a long, straight headwall of squared, dressed stone blocks with a flat coping just above road level, and short wing walls. No railing: the coping is the only edge. Dry, leaf-filled channel in open hardwood forest. The structure dates from the road of 1863 and was refaced when the park roads were improved.

traits.railing_detail: flat stone coping at road level
